::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Aug 11th 1863  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Huntington Library
:::

Dear [Mr Furnivall](people/person_531.qmd)

Thanks for the list of needs of the [letter B](organizations/other_151.qmd). I had been making the like, but found the wants so constantly supplied from the overflowings of your pigeon holes that I grew lazy and desisted.

The printer at Winchester charges 7/6 per 1000 for the titles he prints for us on show paper,[^1] and we have had 4000 - which have chiefly been used by [my mother](people/person_1606.qmd), as I have generally taken mine from the books that did not furnish enough to make it worth while to print their titles.

I am desiring [Parker](people/person_1144.qmd) to send a copy of the [Christian Names](cmy_books/cmybook_48.qmd) to the [Reader](organizations/other_97.qmd). I think he never sends his books widely to reviews, though I never could make out what was the principle of selection as some certainly are sent out. If you are kind enough to review the book, I shall look out for the notice with great interest. I have only had two really useful and improving reviews of it, one in the [Saturday](organizations/other_99.qmd), and one in the [Nonconformist](organizations/other_95.qmd), a good many besides civil and useless. I hope nobody thinks I know all the languages there in referred to! In fact I fear there is plenty of internal evidence that I only got up what I wanted <u>as</u> I wanted it, and that not in the most thorough manner, and that I very much broke down in the correcting of the press.

Yours faithfully

C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Black-edged paper.
[^2]: Presumably slips of paper with the name of the book printed on the top where the usage of each individual word could be added.
